problem: Embodied navigation tasks with different goal modalities (object category, image, text) are usually handled by separate task-specific systems, and RL policies over dense action spaces or with dense rewards are hard to train and biased.
motivation: Real deployment in unknown environments needs one framework that handles multimodal goals robustly. A compact topo-metric graph representation can give a concise action space for sub-goal selection.
key_idea: Build a relative topo-metric intention graph whose frontier nodes and intention nodes form a concise action space for an RL policy, trained with a sparse reward, to select sub-goals for multimodal-goal navigation.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation evidence can be cited. The abstract suggests that a small graph-based action space (frontiers plus intention nodes) with sparse rewards reduces training bias and unifies tasks.
method: Relative topo-metric intention graph: represents the environment as a graph with relative metric information, including intention nodes tied to the multimodal goal.
RL sub-goal policy: selects among frontier nodes and intention nodes as a concise action space.
Sparse reward design: reduces reward-induced bias during training.
Engineering optimizations: several unspecified tweaks to improve overall performance.
